sentence: Reuters reported in May 2025 that engineers found undocumented communication devices inside some mainland-made solar inverters and batteries.
Mainland firms supply a growing share of the inverters and batteries on American grid sites.
The 2017 National Intelligence Law obliges every mainland organization to support the state's intelligence work.
OpenAI said in January 2025 that it had evidence DeepSeek used its models' outputs to train a rival, a practice called distillation.
Anthropic barred companies controlled from the People's Republic from its services in September 2025.
Anthropic named DeepSeek, Moonshot and MiniMax for large-scale distillation on February 23, 2026.
The Commerce Department proposed know-your-customer rules for foreign users of American cloud services in January 2024.
Authorities on the mainland barred a Wells Fargo executive who holds American citizenship from leaving the country in July 2025, and the bank suspended staff travel there.
The State Department warns that the People's Republic uses exit bans against Americans.
American firms still send staff to the mainland without a shared warning system.
Mainland-owned companion apps ranked among the most downloaded AI apps in the United States in 2024.
The Protecting Americans' Data from Foreign Adversaries Act of 2024 bars data brokers from selling Americans' sensitive data to entities controlled by a foreign adversary.
The Justice Department's bulk data rule took effect on April 8, 2025.
The United States completed its withdrawal from the World Health Organization on January 22, 2026.
The World Health Assembly adopted the Pandemic Agreement on May 20, 2025.
The People's Republic pledged $500 million to the organization over five years in May 2025.
The Justice Department charged two researchers from the People's Republic on June 3, 2025 with smuggling the crop fungus Fusarium graminearum into a University of Michigan lab.
The fungus causes head blight in wheat and barley.
American growers already lose heavily to it in wet years.
The mBridge platform links central banks in the People's Republic and Hong Kong with Thailand, the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia.
The Bank for International Settlements left the project in October 2024.
Hong Kong's stablecoin law took effect on August 1, 2025.
The GENIUS Act of July 2025 set federal rules for dollar stablecoins, including the power to freeze funds under lawful order.
The Party enacted the Anti-Foreign Sanctions Law in June 2021, and the Ministry of Commerce issued rules that let mainland parties sue firms that comply with foreign sanctions.
An executive order of December 2023 warned foreign banks that they risk American sanctions for serving Russia's military industry.
The Party has added American defense firms to its unreliable entity list many times since 2023.
A Hong Kong court convicted Jimmy Lai on December 15, 2025 of conspiring to collude with foreign forces and of sedition.
The court sentenced him on February 9, 2026.
Lai holds British citizenship, and Washington and London have both called for his release.
Secretary of State Rubio announced in May 2025 that the United States would revoke visas of mainland students with Party ties or in critical fields.
President Trump said in August 2025 that he would welcome 600,000 mainland students.
American campuses hosted 277,398 mainland students in the 2023 to 2024 academic year.
Texas enacted a law in 2025 that restricts land purchases by entities and some individuals tied to the People's Republic and three other countries.
Florida's 2023 law has faced federal litigation brought by Chinese residents.
The Agriculture Department launched a farm security action plan in July 2025.
CISA, the NSA and the FBI warned on February 7, 2024 that Volt Typhoon had placed itself inside the networks of American critical infrastructure to enable disruption in a crisis.
Some of that access had lasted at least five years.
Microsoft reported in May 2023 that the group targeted infrastructure on Guam.
Mainland labs release open-weight models that rank among the most downloaded in the world.
The American AI Action Plan of July 2025 directed federal evaluators to test mainland models for Party talking points and censorship.
The Commerce Department's AI standards center published an evaluation of DeepSeek models in 2025.
Kinmen has drawn water from Fujian through an undersea pipeline since August 2018.
The island sits two miles off Xiamen and more than a hundred miles from Taiwan's main island.
The Party has proposed a bridge from Xiamen to Kinmen as part of its plans for "integrated development" of Fujian and Taiwan.
TSMC began volume production in Arizona in late 2024 and plans more advanced plants there.
Taiwan still makes most of the world's leading-edge chips.
Surveys in Taiwan have long shown doubt that the United States would fight for the island.
A joint House report of September 12, 2024 found that ZPMC supplied about 80 percent of the ship-to-shore cranes at American ports and that some carried cellular modems no one had ordered.
A February 2024 executive order funded American crane production.
Congress barred the Party's LOGINK logistics platform from ports the military uses.
The Commerce Department eased rules in 2019 and 2024 so American firms could keep working in standards bodies alongside listed mainland companies.
The Party's delegates entered bodies such as the ITU and 3GPP as newcomers and now draft much of the text.
The ITU elects its leadership at plenipotentiary conferences every four years.
Mainland yards build more than half of the world's commercial ships by tonnage, and American yards build under one percent.
Federal law bars the Navy from building its warships in foreign yards.
The United States suspended its port fees on mainland-built ships in November 2025 as part of the trade truce.
Mainland factories install more industrial robots each year than the rest of the world combined.
The Party's Fifteenth Five-Year Plan makes AI and advanced manufacturing central priorities.
The Commerce Department barred mainland software from connected vehicles starting with model year 2027.
The Defense Department's 2026 list of Chinese military companies grew by 65 names.
The Party's military-civil fusion strategy directs civilian research toward military use.
Federal research-security rules since 2021 require disclosure of foreign support and training.
The 2025 tax law cut clean-energy credits for projects that use components from foreign entities of concern.
The Party restricted exports of battery cathode and lithium processing technology in July 2025.
American utilities added large amounts of battery storage in 2024 and 2025, much of it built with mainland cells.
A federal jury convicted a former Google engineer on January 29, 2026 of stealing AI trade secrets for mainland companies.
RAND researchers warned in 2024 that frontier labs could not defend model weights against the best state attackers.
A model's weights hold years of compute and research in a single file.
A Chongqing court set global royalty rates in a patent dispute in December 2023.
Wuhan courts issued anti-suit injunctions in 2020 that barred parties from litigating abroad.
The European Union challenged those injunctions at the World Trade Organization in February 2022.
The Dalai Lama stated on July 2, 2025 that the Gaden Phodrang Trust alone holds authority to recognize his reincarnation.
The Foreign Ministry answered that any successor needs the central government's approval.
The Tibetan Policy and Support Act of 2020 makes it American policy that Tibetan Buddhists alone choose the successor.
The Justice Department charged a former aide to two New York governors in September 2024 with acting as an undisclosed agent of the People's Republic.
The United Front Work Department runs the Party's outreach to foreign officials and communities.
State governments carry no general duty to register agents of foreign principals.
Federal prosecutors charged two men in April 2023 with running an undeclared police station for the Ministry of Public Security in Manhattan, and one pleaded guilty in December 2024.
Safeguard Defenders counted more than 100 such stations worldwide in 2022.
The Justice Department's bulk data rule bars transfers of Americans' sensitive data to entities tied to countries of concern.
The FBI warned in May 2025 that criminals and hostile actors were using AI voice messages to impersonate senior American officials.
The Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity publishes an open standard for content credentials.
Few government agencies attach those credentials to their own video.
Mainland regulators must approve every game sold on the mainland.
The Defense Department listed Tencent as a Chinese military company in January 2025.
Mainland firms hold stakes in major American and European game studios.
Treasury and Commerce have designated hundreds of mainland firms since 2022 for supplying Russia's military industry.
Investigators have found mainland-made components in drones used by Russia and by forces aligned with Iran.
The Party calls its exports ordinary commerce.
The Foreign Agents Registration Act exempts agents who register under the Lobbying Disclosure Act when they represent foreign commercial interests.
The catalog's FARA gap shows that exemption at work from 2017 to 2024.
The Defense Department added 65 companies to its list in June 2026.
Treasury exempted domestic companies from beneficial-ownership reporting under the Corporate Transparency Act in March 2025.
CFIUS reviews foreign investment but depends on filings and on its own search for deals no one filed.
In the Grand Forks case of 2022 and 2023, federal reviewers found they lacked jurisdiction over a land purchase near an Air Force base.
The United States left the World Health Organization on January 22, 2026.
The Party delayed its reports on COVID-19 in December 2019 and January 2020, as the book's COVID chapter documents.
The WHO declared eight public health emergencies of international concern from 2009 through 2024.
The President ordered the Strategic Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients Reserve filled with about 26 critical drugs in August 2025.
The United States imports most of the starting materials for its generic drugs, many from the mainland or from Indian makers that rely on mainland inputs.
The heparin contamination of 2008 showed the risk of long and opaque drug supply chains.
The BIOSECURE Act became law on December 18, 2025.
The Justice Department's bulk data rule took effect on April 8, 2025 and bars transfers of Americans' genomic data to countries of concern.
Reporting in 2021 found that BGI developed its prenatal test with the PLA and sold it in more than fifty countries.
S&P rated the developer Vanke in selective default in December 2025.
Property investment on the mainland fell 19.9 percent in the first eight months of 2026.
Most mainland companies listed in the United States use variable interest entities, contracts that give foreign shareholders no ownership of the operating firm.
Mainland holdings of Treasury securities peaked at more than $1.3 trillion in 2013 and have fallen by nearly half since.
A fire sale would cut the value of the Party's own reserves and push the yuan up against the exporters it protects.
The Federal Reserve keeps standing repo facilities and swap lines for market stress.
The allies froze about half of Russia's central bank reserves in 2022.
The People's Bank has reported gold purchases in most months since late 2022, and its reported reserves stood near 2,300 tonnes in 2025.
Analysts estimate that the Party's real holdings exceed the reported figure.
Hong Kong's stablecoin law took effect on August 1, 2025.
The Hong Kong Autonomy Act of 2020 lets Washington sanction banks that deal with officials who undermine the city's autonomy.
Treasury's reports under that act named no bank from 2020 to 2022.
The Privacy and Civil Liberties Oversight Board has lacked a quorum since January 2025.
Its one remaining member has served past her term since January 29, 2026.

The State Department began reviewing the social media of every student visa applicant in June 2025, and agencies score travelers, applicants and employees with automated tools built on purchased data.
The Justice Department ended its China Initiative in February 2022.
MIT Technology Review found that 130 of the 148 people charged under it were of Chinese heritage.
A study in PNAS found that departures of scientists of Chinese descent from the United States rose from about 900 in 2010 to 2,621 in 2021.
House appropriators wrote language to restore the initiative in September 2025 and dropped it in January 2026.
The Party's export controls grew from gallium and germanium in 2023 to graphite, antimony and seven heavy rare earths by April 2025.
Its October 2025 rules reached any product in the world with 0.1 percent or more of mainland rare earth content, and the Party suspended them under the trade truce until November 10, 2026.
The licensing of heavy rare earths never lapsed, and the general licenses issued from December 2025 exclude defense and aerospace buyers.
NIST published its first three post-quantum encryption standards in August 2024.
Its draft transition plan of November 2024 would deprecate RSA and elliptic-curve keys after 2030 and disallow them after 2035, and it remained a draft in August 2026.
The University of Science and Technology of China ran a 105-qubit processor, Zuchongzhi 3.0, in 2025.
Researchers at Duke University bought data on active-duty service members from brokers in 2023 for as little as 12 cents a record.
Congress barred brokers in 2024 from selling Americans' sensitive data to foreign adversaries, including location data and military status.
The FTC sent warning letters under that law to 13 brokers in February 2026.
Shijian-21 towed a dead Beidou satellite to a graveyard orbit in January 2022.
Shijian-25 docked with Shijian-21 in geostationary orbit in July 2025 for the first apparent refueling there.
The two separated on November 25, 2025.
The Space Force's vice chief said in March 2025 that five mainland satellites had practiced dogfighting in low orbit.
Artemis II flew four astronauts around the Moon in April 2026, and NASA moved its first landing to Artemis IV, targeted for 2028.
The Party aims to land astronauts by 2030 and postponed its Chang'e-7 south-pole probe to 2027 after a scrub on August 24, 2026.
Seventy-six nations had signed the Artemis Accords by September 25, 2026.
The President ordered a missile shield for the homeland in January 2025, and its program lead later put the cost at about $185 billion.
The Congressional Budget Office estimated in May 2026 that a system meeting the order could cost $1.2 trillion over 20 years, most of it for about 7,800 interceptors in orbit.
The Pentagon reported in December 2025 that the mainland's stockpile stood in the low 600s and would exceed 1,000 by 2030.
Data centers used 4.7 percent of American electricity in 2024, and a Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory report of June 2026 projects 9.5 to 15.3 percent by 2030.
The mainland's installed generating capacity reached about 3,960 gigawatts in March 2026, up 15.5 percent in a year.
Washington allowed sales of Nvidia's H200 chips to the mainland in December 2025 in exchange for a 25 percent share of the revenue.
The two presidents agreed in November 2024 that humans, not AI, should control decisions to use nuclear weapons.
During Xi Jinping's state visit in September 2026 the two governments launched what the White House called the Super Intelligence Dialogue, with a channel for reporting incidents.
They set its next meeting for November 2026.
The PLA declined a call from the Secretary of Defense during the balloon crisis of February 2023.
Taiwan's cabinet proposed NT$1.12 trillion for defense in 2027, or 3.01 percent of GDP, down from 3.32 percent in 2026.
The legislature passed a special arms act of NT$780 billion in May 2026, well short of the NT$1.25 trillion the government sought.
President Lai Ching-te has pledged to reach 5 percent of GDP by 2030.
In the Election Study Center's survey at National Chengchi University, 62.0 percent of Taiwan's people identified as Taiwanese only in December 2025.
The Party's rules for generative AI require services to uphold core socialist values.
Alibaba's Qwen models were the most downloaded model family on Hugging Face in 2025.
The mainland's youth unemployment rate reached 18.9 percent in August 2026.
The China Coast Guard has patrolled the waters around Kinmen since February 2024, after two mainland fishermen died fleeing a Taiwanese patrol boat.
Kinmen lies within sight of Xiamen.
The Party declared itself a near-Arctic state in its white paper of January 2018.
The Coast Guard reported five mainland research vessels operating in the American Arctic in August 2025.
Russian and mainland coast guard ships patrolled together in the Bering Sea in October 2024.
Huawei reported revenue of CNY 880.9 billion for 2025 and spent CNY 192.3 billion on research, about 22 percent of revenue.
The Party has financed digital networks across Asia, Africa and Latin America under its Digital Silk Road since 2015.
Western vendors compete country by country and rarely offer financing on the same terms.
A Navy intelligence estimate in 2023 put mainland shipbuilding capacity at about 232 times America's.
The FCC added foreign-made drones and their components to its Covered List on December 22, 2025.
Commerce suspended its rule extending export controls to affiliates of listed firms for one year in November 2025 under the trade truce.
A Federal Reserve note of September 25, 2026 found that new American greenfield projects in China fell sharply after 2020 and never recovered.
The same note found that dividends from American subsidiaries there now exceed reinvestment.
The IMF put the mainland's augmented government debt at 126.6 percent of GDP in 2025.
The Australian Strategic Policy Institute found in December 2025 that mainland institutions led research in 66 of 74 critical technologies.
The mainland's largest academic database, CNKI, restricted foreign access to several collections in 2023.
The Party expelled American reporters from three newspapers in 2020.
Deferred Enforced Departure shields eligible Hong Kong residents in the United States through February 5, 2027.
Freedom House counted the Party as the source of 272 of 1,219 physical incidents of transnational repression from 2014 through 2024.
Encounters with mainland nationals at the southern border rose sharply in 2023 and 2024.
Freedom House named the Party the most prolific perpetrator of transnational repression, with 22 percent of recorded physical incidents from 2014 through 2024.
The Justice Department charged two men in April 2023 with running an undeclared police station for the Party in Manhattan.
Leaked Xinjiang police files in 2022 showed registries that tracked families and travel in detail.
A study in Nature Human Behaviour in May 2025 found that GPT-4, given personal data about its opponents, persuaded better than human debaters 64 percent of the time.
OpenAI reported in 2025 that operations likely linked to the People's Republic had used ChatGPT to write social media posts and internal reports.
No federal law requires disclosure of AI-generated content in political ads, although about 30 states regulate election deepfakes.
Ne Zha 2 earned about $2.26 billion worldwide in 2025 and about $23 million in North America.
A Beijing-based publisher listed in Shenzhen owns 49 percent of the company behind ReelShort, a short-drama app that earned about $130 million worldwide in the first quarter of 2025.
Short dramas reach American audiences through phones rather than theaters.
Hugging Face reported in August 2026 that developers had built 151,448 derivative models on Alibaba's Qwen, 2.6 times the count built on Meta's models.
The Party's rules for generative AI of 2023 require services to uphold core socialist values.
Open models cost little to run, and poorer governments can adapt them without license fees.
The Houthis attacked more than 100 merchant ships from November 2023 to mid-2025 and sank four.

The State Department said in April 2025 that Chang Guang Satellite Technology supported Houthi attacks, and Treasury sanctioned three mainland firms among 32 targets in a Houthi network in September 2025.
The Houthis told Beijing and Moscow in 2024 that their ships would pass unharmed.
The FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center logged more than 3,600 ransomware complaints in 2025, up from 3,156 in 2024.
The ransomware attack on Change Healthcare in 2024 exposed data on 192.7 million people.
Anthropic reported in November 2025 that a state-sponsored group it tied to the People's Republic used AI agents for 80 to 90 percent of an espionage campaign against about 30 organizations.
ChemChina bought the seed and crop chemical company Syngenta for $43 billion in 2017.
Arkansas ordered Syngenta Seeds in October 2023 to sell 160 acres of farmland and later collected a $280,000 fine.
The USDA counted 247,659 acres of American farmland held by Chinese investors at the end of 2024.
The CIA judged in January 2025, with low confidence, that a lab origin for COVID-19 was more likely than a natural one.
The WHO's advisory group said in June 2025 that the evidence it had favored spillover from animals, and that it could not settle the question without data the mainland had withheld.
The World Health Assembly has not yet adopted the pathogen-sharing annex to its pandemic agreement.
The mainland's Cross-Border Interbank Payment System processed RMB 180.15 trillion in 2025, up about 3 percent from 2024.
SWIFT's July 2026 tracker put the yuan at 3.10 percent of international payments outside the eurozone, fifth among currencies.
The dollar held about 50 percent.
The IMF put the mainland's augmented government debt at 126.6 percent of GDP in 2025 and projected 150 percent by 2029.
A Hong Kong court ordered Evergrande's liquidation in January 2024.
Property investment on the mainland fell 19.9 percent in the first eight months of 2026.
The Basic Law promises that Hong Kong's system stays unchanged for fifty years, through June 30, 2047.
The Party imposed a national security law on the city on June 30, 2020, and Hong Kong passed its own security law in March 2024.
A Hong Kong court sentenced the publisher Jimmy Lai to 20 years in prison on February 9, 2026.
Mainland visitors bought HK$62.8 billion of new Hong Kong insurance policies in 2024, 28.6 percent of new individual business.
Hong Kong's Insurance Authority has published no separate figure for mainland visitors since early 2025.
Britain has granted well over 100,000 visas to Hong Kongers with British National (Overseas) status since 2021.
Federal agencies reported more than 1,700 AI use cases in their 2024 inventories, about double the year before.
Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act lapsed on June 12, 2026, after Congress failed to renew it.
The Privacy and Civil Liberties Oversight Board has lacked a quorum since January 2025.
The Brennan Center counted 52 national emergencies in effect on September 16, 2026.
Presidents renew them each year without a vote in Congress.
The Supreme Court struck down tariffs imposed under emergency powers on February 20, 2026.
A 2020 indictment charged four members of the People's Liberation Army with stealing records on about 145 million Americans from Equifax in 2017.
The breach of the Office of Personnel Management in 2015 exposed files on 21.5 million people.
CISA reported in 2024 that the Volt Typhoon group had prepositioned itself inside American infrastructure.
The China Cables of 2019 and the Xinjiang Police Files of 2022 showed what leaked Party records can prove.
A hacker offered data on about one billion residents from a Shanghai police database for sale in 2022.
Wang Lijun's flight to the American consulate in Chengdu in 2012 exposed the crimes that brought down Bo Xilai.
The Party expelled Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli on September 21, 2026, leaving Xi Jinping and Zhang Shengmin as the only members of the Central Military Commission.
The Pentagon reported in December 2025 that the mainland's arsenal would exceed 1,000 warheads by 2030.
New START expired on February 5, 2026, and the Party rejected American calls for trilateral nuclear talks.
The mainland plans two low-orbit constellations, Guowang with about 13,000 satellites and Qianfan with about 14,000.
It flew more than 90 orbital launches in 2025, a national record.
Together the two constellations had only a few hundred satellites in orbit by 2026.
The PLA's white paper of 2019 named intelligentized warfare as the direction of military change.
DeepSeek released a model in January 2025 that matched leading American systems at a fraction of the reported training cost.
The two governments opened a dialogue on superintelligence in September 2026, and the White House ruled out joint regulation of frontier models.
Researchers at Fudan University reported in December 2024 that two open models copied themselves when told to do so in experiments.
Commerce proposed in January 2024 that American cloud providers verify the identity of foreign customers.
Hourly compute rentals still require little proof of who or what is paying.
A presidential memorandum of June 5, 2026 ordered the Pentagon to revise its directive on autonomy in weapon systems within 90 days.
The directive, last updated in January 2023, requires appropriate human judgment over the use of force.
The Pentagon awarded contracts worth up to $200 million each to four AI companies in July 2025.
